description: Any eligible US stock. Second-order effects: events traced to a company the news never names.

trades.thesis: TJX beat and raised on 11-18 (comps +4% vs plan 2-3%, FY comp now 4%, Marmaxx improved) and Target posted +5.6% comps on +5% traffic. US control retail sales came in at +0.6% vs 0.4%. Ross reports Q3 on 11-19 after the close with 8 straight EPS beats and comps of +7% and +10% in the last two quarters. It fell 4 days into the print and has lagged TJX's rebound. The edge is Ross's own print, since the sympathy gap is already in the fill price.

causal_chain.step: TJX Q3 FY27 (11-18 BMO): comps +4% vs 2-3% plan and 3.8% consensus, FY comp raised to 4%, Marmaxx improved. Target comps +5.6% on +5.0% traffic. Both show strong off-price and value traffic in the Aug-Oct quarter.

Ross competes for the same shopper as Marmaxx, and its quarter ended around Oct 31. Core retail sales beat (+0.6% vs 0.4%), so the same demand should show in Ross's Q3 comps. Ross has beaten EPS 8 of 8 quarters, with consensus EPS about $1.85 on $6.2B revenue.

ROST reports 11-19 after the close, and the reaction lands in my 3-day horizon. Weakest link: TJX's Marmaxx comp was only +2%, so strength may not transfer to Ross. The sympathy gap at today's open is already in my fill price.

Read-through from strong CTV/political demand suggests upside risk to PubMatic's guide; small size because earnings are binary and PUBM's mix differs.

sessions.feedback:
1) economic_calendar did not populate actuals at 13:33 UTC even though the 08:30 ET releases (PCE, GDP) were already out. Its time column is labelled New York but looks like UTC. I had to find the PCE numbers through a web_search snippet. A refresh, or a correct timezone label, would help.
2) get_quotes pre-market data lags about 15 minutes, so at 13:33 UTC the quote predates the 13:30 UTC PCE release. A 'data as of' warning near scheduled releases would help me avoid trading around binary events.
3) read_page fails on many news domains (invezz, kfgo, foxbusiness). That is acceptable because search snippets carry the numbers, but a list of domains known to work would save calls.
4) The 'no ticker in digest headlines' rule combined with pre-open fills means that by the time I see a story, the first-order and sympathy moves are already in the pre-market price. That makes my second-order approach hard to execute on same-day news; the dated-catalyst route (events after the next open) is the only one with an edge.

No blocking issues. Two small requests. (1) Pre-market prices for scan/get_quotes come with a lag, and the open auction price is unknown, so for names that gap on overnight news (SPY -1.5% since the close) I am sizing off stale numbers. (2) An earnings calendar for the coming week, with BMO/AMC and consensus, would save several web searches. The scan 'earnings' field only covers the last two sessions and the next five, and sometimes shows 'time not given'. Also, scan labels SHOE's earnings as 'none' although it reported this morning, so that field misses same-day reports for some tickers.

The research budget ran out before I could write my notes file, so tomorrow's session starts from this summary and the old notes. A small allowance for a notes update after the budget message would help. read_page failed on Yahoo Finance article URLs again. ETFs such as SPY and QQQ don't appear to be tradable, so I can't express a clean market-beta view. A tool that returned a live intraday market snapshot would help on volatile gap days.

Nothing blocked me this session. Two small things: read_page on prnewswire returned only navigation and no release body, so I had to rely on web_search snippets from the code tool. It would also help to know whether a stop that gaps through at the open fills at the open price or at the stop price. That decides whether closing manually into a gap beats letting the stop work.

Nothing blocked me, but two things would help.
1. The digest and news feed lag same-morning earnings. WSM, BABA and WMT prints were only in the news feed or web search, and I had to use web_search to find the WSM numbers. An earnings-results feed with EPS/revenue vs consensus and guidance for companies that reported pre-market would save calls.
2. scan shows pre-market only as a percent and a share count. An indication of whether the pre-market print is from IEX only or all venues would help me judge thin prints.

No blocking problems this session. Two things would have saved time. First, an earnings-consensus field (EPS and revenue expectations, and the typical post-earnings move) in scan, because I had to run web searches for it. Second, a sympathy-gap estimate: pre-market prints under 1,000 shares are too thin to judge the fill price for a read-through trade, and orders fill at the open, so I can't tell how much of the move I'll pay for. web_search is only reachable from inside code_execution and returns a JSON string, which costs extra calls. read_page on Benzinga still fails.

Digest 'biggest pre-market movers' ranks thin prints (100-600 shares) by sd, so most of the list is noise (e.g., KNX -8.5% on 396 shares). Filtering on minimum shares or a percent-of-average-day threshold would save budget. A tool returning the biggest losers and gainers of the previous session (not only gainers) would help find overreactions. A 'peers with earnings dates in the next 5 days' lookup by industry would suit the lagging-peer strategy.

Benzinga pages usually fail in read_page, though the digest links mostly point to Benzinga. Pre-market lists mix thin prints with real moves (e.g. NX -19% in the news roundup versus 0.0% in scan). Some prices look like spin-off artifacts (CTVA 9.43, -90% from 52-week high); a flag for corporate actions would help.

read_page fails on many major sites (CNBC, NBC, gurufocus), which makes the two-source requirement hard. The sandbox does not keep Python state between code_execution cells, so imports have to be repeated in every cell. A pre-market quote that shows volume (e.g. 828 shares) makes thin-volume REIT quotes misleading; a flag for low-volume pre-market prints would help.

The digest has no sector or industry-level sympathy view and the scan's industry labels are coarse (e.g. UBER/LYFT listed as 'Business Services'). Web search returns stale results for some queries. Earnings-call transcripts or a news-by-ticker endpoint would help.

summary:
Session 2026-11-25.

Session 2026-11-25. No trades; 100% cash (equity about $100.5k).

Tape: SPY pre-market -1.95%, QQQ -2.9%, VIXY +9%. Two drivers: (1) WSJ says USTR will unveil Section 301 overcapacity findings on 16 economies as soon as this week. These include Taiwan, Korea, Japan, EU, Mexico, India, Vietnam, Malaysia, Thailand, Cambodia and Bangladesh. Semis fell 6-11% on 11-24 (TXN -11% on its Malaysia assembly, MU -11%, SNDK -11%, MRVL -9%). (2) The AI de-rating continues. Oct PCE was in line (headline 3.8% y/y; core 0.3% m/m, 3.3% y/y vs 3.2% cons), so there was no macro shock.

DELL resolved my 11-24 conditional. Revenue was $54.9B vs $49.3B, EPS was 9.45 vs 6.60, the FY27 guide was raised, the buyback was $25B, and AI orders were flat QoQ with credit review of neoclouds. The stock still fell 5.6% pre-market after -11.8% on 11-24. HPE was -16.3% on 11-24 and -4.5% pre-market. Fundamentals-based dip buys have no edge until the tape stabilises, so no HPE or DELL long.

Leads examined and rejected:
- Neocloud shorts (CRWV 39.8, NBIS 82): already at the range lows after -10 to -12% days, so the payoff is poor.
- Section 301 beneficiaries (NUE, STLD, FSLR, WHR, INTC): no product list or rates yet, and nothing moved relative to the market pre-market.
- Pharma and biotech rotation (XLV +2.95%, XBI +6.6% on 11-24, SNY +11% on the Insmed deal): day-2 chase with no stock-specific news.
- URBN -12%: brand-specific (Anthropologie comps 1.7%, markdowns, soft Q4 guide).
- AMBA -34% (Q4 revenue guide $70-75M vs $115M in Q3): $1.2B cap, 0.5% slippage, no clean peer chain.
- NTNX: CEO exit plus BofA downgrade, thin print.
- Energy E&Ps: moves are roughly priced.
- HPQ +2.5% pre-market: already moved.
- ANT: 78 pre-market and the stabilisation bid at 83 is gone, but there is no clean edge before the Dec 11-18 NDX flows.

Notes updated: general notes, plus DELL and HPE ticker notes.

Next session (Fri 11-27, after Thanksgiving; the half-day is Friday):
- Check whether the Section 301 list and rates were published (the WSJ said as soon as this week). If so, trade the domestic-producer winners against the importer losers.
- Watch for stabilisation: AI names closing in the upper half of the range and QQQ holding a gap-up. If that happens, consider HPE or DELL longs at about 8x EPS.
- Neocloud shorts only after a squeeze to CRWV 55+ or NBIS 110.
- Dated catalysts: AEO, FIVE and M on 12-02, NTAP and MRVL on 12-01, the Dec 9 FOMC hike, the ANT quiet period around 12-14 and the NDX announcement on 12-11.
notes:
NOTES (updated 2026-11-25)
- Tooling: web_search only works via code_execution and returns a JSON STRING (json.loads it; IMPORT json IN EVERY CELL; results are dicts with title/url/content/page_age). Benzinga/nikkei/bbntimes/substack/marketscreener/invezz/kfgo/foxbusiness read_page usually FAIL; web_search snippet of the same page often carries the numbers (foxbusiness snippet gave PCE). longbridge, factrail, yahoo finance, investing.com, 247wallst, baystreet, tradingview, sec.gov exhibits mostly read OK. get_quotes/get_history/search_symbols/scan/news work directly. scan's pre-market % on <1,000 shares is noise. get_quotes 'pre-market' lags ~15 min; IEX last trade is fresher. economic_calendar 'actual' column did NOT refresh at 13:33 UTC even though 08:30 ET data was out (times in the table are UTC, mislabeled NY): use web_search for actuals. Digest 'top pre-market movers' are often thin prints. Code rejects trades whose names appear in digest HEADLINES. Earnings-day shortcut: news() on tickers gives press-release numbers at ~12:30 UTC.
- Macro regime (Nov 2026): 10y ~5.1%, Fed funds 3.75-4.00, Dec 9 hike priced ~97%. Oct PCE (11-25): headline 0.3% m/m 3.8% y/y (in line), core 0.3% m/m 3.3% y/y (cons 3.2%; Bowman had flagged 3.3%) = no shock. Iran war since late Feb, oil cooling since midterms (Brent ~$90, gas $3.61, -15% m/m), consumer confidence highest since Jan 2025. AI-bust phase: SMH -35% from June high, NVDA -32% from high, neoclouds -65 to -80%, DELL -54% ($595 to ~275), MU -50% from high, SNDK -73%, WDC -66%.
- 11-25 NEW CATALYST: WSJ 11-24: USTR Greer to unveil Section 301 'overcapacity/subsidy' findings on 16 economies (China, EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Mexico, India, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Cambodia, Bangladesh, Singapore, Switzerland, Norway) 'as soon as this week' (Philippines already pays 12.5% under a separate 301 since July). Semis hit 11-24: TXN -11.2% (Malaysia assembly), MU -11%, SNDK -11%, MRVL -9%, SKHY -10%, INTC -8%, GFS -6.5%; pre-market 11-25 SPY -1.95%, QQQ -2.9%, VIXY +9%. Also Trump 11-24 said he has considered a US gov equity stake in NVDA and a Huang pardon is 'an option'. No product list/rates yet, so beneficiaries (steel NUE/STLD, solar FSLR, appliances WHR) are unproven and did not move pre-market.
- ROTATION: 11-24 health care led (XLV +2.95%, XBI +6.6%, big pharma +3-5% on no stock news; Sanofi-Insmed $41B deal 'largest since 2023', SNY +11%), staples +1.7%. Pharma flat-to-up pre-market 11-25 while QQQ -2.9%: money leaving chips for defensives. Not traded (day-2 chase).
- DELL (11-24 AMC): rev 54.9B (+103%, cons 49.3B), EPS 9.45 vs 6.60, FY27 EPS 29.68, AI backlog 132.3B, AI orders 60.2B flat QoQ (60.9B in Q2), $25B buyback, selective on neocloud credit; stock closed -11.8% BEFORE print, +0.9% AH, -5.6% pre-market (~8x FY28 EPS, ~10% shareholder yield). HPE -16.3% on 11-24 (pre-market had been -12%: the day was worse than pre-market). Sector de-rating confirmed: no HPE/DELL long edge yet. HPQ +2.5% pre-market on FY27 EPS guide 3.15-3.45 (PC side holding).
- BOUNCE-FADE PATTERN: AI names opened at the high on 11-23 and closed in the bottom 15% (NBIS open 110 = high, close 97.8). 11-24 close: NBIS 87.3, CRWV 42.6 (pre-market 39.8, at the 40-day low 39.3), ANT 81.9 (below $83 IPO; pre-market 78). Beat-and-raise gets sold in this tape (HPE, ADI, DELL); low-bar misses get bought (BURL).
- Anthropic (ANT): IPO $83, day-1 close 97.17, 11-20 low 83.05 (= stabilization bid), now 78-82 so underwriter support is gone. NDX fast entry: announcement after close Dec 11, entry Dec 21 (funds buy at close Dec 18). Quiet-period expiry ~Dec 14. SpaceX precedent: no pre-inclusion run-up, -15% in 6 sessions after joining. Not traded.
- Retail: DKS, DLTR, BBY, ANF strong 11-24; URBN -12% (record Q3 but Anthropologie comps 1.7%, markdowns, soft Q4, MS downgrade: brand-specific). Peer sympathy moves are priced by pre-open. Upcoming: AEO 12-02 AMC, FIVE 12-02, M 12-02 BMO, DG early Dec, NKE ~Dec 18. IEEPA refunds boost EPS but retailers reinvest in price.
- M&A: Sanofi buys Insmed $175 cash (close H1 2027), INSM ~170.7: 2.5% spread, no trade.
- Health insurers: CMS CRUSH proposed rule (RADV back to PY2018, ~$9B/yr, comments to 1-19-2027). UNH -18% over 5d, +1.7% 11-24. Not traded.
- Trades so far: PUBM (11-06 long 4%, closed 11-13 +12.5%, +9.9 pts vs SPY). ROST (11-18 long 4% at 226.23, closed 11-20 around 208, about -8%). No-trade sessions: 10-29, 11-04, 11-16, 11-17, 11-19, 11-20, 11-23, 11-24, 11-25. Cash equity ~$100.5k (cash has beaten SPY since 11-20).
- LESSONS:
 1) Peer-earnings-lag longs: PUBM worked (dated catalyst, peer lagged), ROST failed (11-18 buy -> 11-20 print). Retail print reactions follow the NEXT-quarter guide, not the FY raise. Avoid buying into a peer's print after a run-down in a falling tape.
 2) By the pre-open session, first-order and obvious second-order moves are priced (GDS -14.7% a day before I looked; cyber peers +4-6% pre-market on PANW; retail sympathy 11-24; TXN -11% on the Section 301 Malaysia chain, pharma rotation). The sympathy gap is in the fill price. Real edge needs dated catalysts AHEAD of the next session.
 3) Regulatory proposals (CRUSH) and big-cap drops can stay down for months: need a catalyst, not just a drop (UNH Jan-2026 analog).
 4) In capitulation tapes pre-open 'bounce' longs are coin flips; wait for stabilisation (VIX peak, index holding a gap-up).
 5) When binary info arrives BEFORE my next open (PCE 11-25, DELL AMC 11-24), waiting a day is cheaper than holding through it. On 11-25 PCE resolved as in-line (no shock) and DELL's beat was still sold: macro/tariff/AI-credit sentiment dominates fundamentals, so fundamentals-based dip buys have no edge until the tape stabilises.
 6) Pre-market prints understate continuation on gap-down days for post-earnings AI names (HPE -12% pre, -16.3% close); do not assume the pre-market is the low.
- Open ideas: Section 301 beneficiaries/losers once rates and product lists are published (domestic steel/aluminum/solar/appliances/US fabs INTC TXN GFS vs importers with Vietnam/Cambodia/Bangladesh apparel exposure); HPE/DELL long only after a stabilised tape (8x EPS, buybacks); neocloud shorts only after a squeeze to the upper range (CRWV 55+, NBIS 110); ANT around Dec 11-18; NDX funds sell other mega-caps to fund ANT (mid-Dec); tower churn (AMT/CCI/SBAC); JBS/China beef quotas; MA-exposed clinic landlords; TREE; NKE into Dec 18; DG into early Dec print; biotech M&A read-across after Sanofi/Insmed (look for similar rare-respiratory commercial-stage names); energy E&Ps as Hormuz risk fades (XLE only -4.6% 5d vs Brent -22% 4w; not yet shorted).

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is weird, second-order research.

Everyone else reads the headline and trades the company in it. You trade the company the headline
does not mention. Start from events in the news and follow the consequences outward: suppliers,
customers, competitors, substitutes, regions, commodities, logistics, weather, regulation, the
odd dependency nobody has priced. A storm hits the region that grows potatoes for a fast-food chain;
which other chain gains, which frozen-food maker loses, which railroad hauls the replacement crop?

- Every new position, long or short, needs a causal chain of at least two steps from the event to
  the company you trade, each step with a source where possible. Code rejects a trade whose ticker
  or company name appears in today's digest headlines, so the link has to be one you found. The
  losers at the end of a chain are as fair game as the winners: short them.
- Borderline delusional is the brief, but the chain still has to be real: each step should be
  something you could defend with evidence. Write down the step most likely to be wrong.
- Spreading across several smaller bets suits this style better than one big one. Small companies
  cost more to trade, so make the expected move worth it.
- Use search_symbols to find the companies at the end of a chain. Read their exposure, do not assume it.
